text:
Logan Cooley did almost everything a player can do in one night: three goals, an assist, and more wins added by our measure than anyone on either team. He still went home with a loss, because Montreal kept answering, a 2022 draft pick scored his first NHL goal at the perfect moment, and Cole Caufield needed 30 seconds of overtime to finish it 5-4.

Cooley put Utah up 2-0 inside the first 9:24, once at even strength and once on the power play. Nick Suzuki got the Canadiens on the board at 15:25, and Arber Xhekaj tied it at 17:10 with a slap shot that had a 2% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the night. Cooley's third, another power-play snap shot at 11:05 of the second, restored the lead and completed the hat trick.

Kirby Dach tied it 1:09 into the third on a power play, finishing a 62% chance. Nick Schmaltz put Utah back in front at 7:14, again with the man advantage. Utah's power play went 3 for 5, and that is how a team with 20 shots on goal scores four. Sebastian Cossa kept the lead alive at 13:33 when he stopped Caufield on a 25% look.

Then Adam Engstrom, the 92nd pick in 2022, scored his first NHL goal at 14:54 off a 6% snap shot, assisted by Jake Evans and Noah Dobson. Montreal's chance of winning went from 14% to 52% in one shot. In overtime Lane Hutson and Suzuki fed Caufield, and that was that.

Montreal earned it. The Canadiens took 69 shot attempts to Utah's 56, won the third period 1.86 to 0.91 in expected goals, and would win this game 64% of the time if every shot were replayed. Suzuki had a goal and two assists, Hutson played 27 minutes with two assists, and the Canadiens generated 2.48 expected goals on their own power play, even if only one went in. Even strength was dead level at 2.01 each, which tells you where Utah's offense came from. Cooley's three goals came from 0.71 expected goals of his own, a night of finishing that won't happen every week, and a reminder of why a 3rd overall pick gets the benefit of the doubt.
headline: Cooley's hat trick isn't enough as Montreal storms back
